diagnostic_evidence.quote: By the Burkholder--Gundy--Davis inequality \cite[Theorem 3.28]{Karatzas1991-xr}, for a constant $c$,
By \cref{cor}, the $\mathbb{E} \bp{\pp{\int_s^t\frac{1}{|u_r|^{2-\epsilon}} \,dr}^q}$ is finite for $\epsilon>0$ and $q\ge 1$.

issues.failure_explanation: BDG gives E|∫u^{ε-1}dW|^q ≤ c E[(∫u^{2ε-2}dt)^{q/2}], not c(∫E[u^{2ε-2}]dt)^{q/2}. For q>2, Jensen gives E[X^{q/2}] ≥ (EX)^{q/2}, so the displayed bound does not follow. Part 1 only controls first moments of u^{2ε-2}, so part 2 is established only for q≤2. Bounding E[(∫u^{2ε-2})^{q/2}] is itself a higher moment of an inverse-power time integral, which is the quantity part 2 is trying to bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a localization (stopping at u≤δ) and bootstrap argument. Use u^{2ε-2} ≤ 1+u^{ε-2} to obtain E X^q ≤ C + C(E X^q)^{1/2} for X=∫u^{ε-2}, then let δ→0.
issues.overall_effect: Part 2 of the corollary is unproven for q>2. The time-regularity proposition needs arbitrarily high moments of ∫u^{-(2-ε)}, and with it the whole strong-convergence chain loses support.
issues.title: BDG inequality misapplied for q>2 in inverse-moment integral bound
issues.why_classification: The repair needs a contained new argument (localization plus self-improving estimate) but no new architecture; all stated conclusions survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The third factor is $O(|t-s|^{\epsilon/2})$ by part 1.

issues.failure_explanation: The singular drift ∫1/u is bounded via Hölder by |t-s|^{(1-ε)/(2-ε)}, which is strictly below 1/2. The proof therefore concludes only (E|u_t-u_s|^q)^{1/q} ≤ c|t-s|^{1/2-ε}, yet the statement asserts |t-s|^{q/2}. Part 2 and later estimates (e.g. the Δt^{3/2} term for r_{1,k}) then use the unproven full 1/2 rate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate part 1 as E‖z_t−z_s‖^q ≤ c|t−s|^{q(1/2−ε)} and propagate the ε-loss through part 2 and the remainder estimates. The stated downstream rates Δt^{1/2−ε} survive after renaming ε.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed optimal Hölder-1/2 moment regularity is unsupported. Downstream exponents (part 2, the remainder bounds in the error propositions) must be re-tracked with an extra ε loss.
issues.title: Time-regularity part 1 claims rate q/2 but proof gives only q(1/2-ε)
issues.why_classification: The stated rate of part 1 is lost and must be weakened. Downstream results survive only after re-tracking exponents.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By \cite[Corollary 5.14]{Karatzas1991-xr}, it is enough to find an $\epsilon>0$ such that, for all $t\in [0,T]$,
the condition on $\alpha$ is satisfied if

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds exponential moments only over short windows of length ε < βλ/(2γB²), because the Lyapunov computation needs α<βλ. The cited Karatzas criterion (local Novikov on a partition) yields only that the Girsanov exponential is a martingale. It does not yield E exp(γ∫_0^T‖b‖²) < ∞ for all γ,T. Since π has Gaussian tails exp(−βλ‖z‖²/2), the Jensen-based method cannot produce the global claim for large γT, so it remains unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the lemma as the local (short-window) exponential bound, hence that the Girsanov density is a true martingale, and drop the global claim for all γ and T.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed integrability claim of the lemma is unsupported. The Girsanov/positivity use and the strong Feller proposition need only the martingale property, which is still established.
issues.title: Novikov lemma asserts global exponential moments that the proof does not give
issues.why_classification: The lemma's stated quantitative content must be withdrawn and weakened, although its downstream use survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: standard theory (Bakry--Emery criterion, Holley--Stroock theorem) applies to the potential $\frac 12 \lambda \|\vec x \|^2+G_3(\vec x)$, as it is a bounded perturbation

issues.failure_explanation: The invariant measure is ∝ exp(−β(½λ‖x‖²+G_3)). The bounded perturbation is βG_3, whose oscillation is β(sup G − inf G). Holley–Stroock therefore gives the LSI constant βλ e^{−β(sup G−inf G)}, not βλ e^{−(sup G−inf G)}. For β>1 the stated rate is faster than what the cited theory supports.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace R by βλ exp(−β(sup G − inf G)).
issues.overall_effect: The explicit exponential rate in the entropy decay estimate is overstated for β>1. Geometric convergence itself is unaffected.
issues.title: LSI constant omits β in the Holley–Stroock factor
issues.why_classification: A local constant correction gives the right rate; the qualitative geometric ergodicity result and the method are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $(u^0,v^0)$ and $(u(0),v(0))$ follow an initial distribution $\rho_0\ll \pi $ such that $\frac{\rho_0}{\pi}$ is uniformly bounded.
this error converges to zero by \cref{thm:num_conv} as $\tstep\to 0$ with $T=k\,\tstep$
For example, let $\tilde{\pi}_\tstep(\cdot)=\pi_\tstep(\cdot \cap B_R) /\pi_\tstep(B_R)$ for the ball $B_R$ of radius $R=\tstep^{-1}$).

issues.failure_explanation: The finite-time convergence theorem is qualitative and holds for a fixed initial law ρ0 with ρ0/π bounded. Its constants (via the corollary and time-regularity bounds) depend on ‖ρ0/π‖. The proof applies it with initial law π_Δt or its truncation, which changes with Δt, so uniformity over that family is required and not shown. Nor is it shown that the truncated law has bounded density ratio with respect to π, uniformly or at all, especially since the radius R=1/Δt grows. The truncated law is also not invariant for the chain, so the step replacing π_Δt(φ) needs a further unproved comparison. The stated decomposition π_Δt(φ)−π(φ)=E_{1,T}+E_2(T) does not hold as written.

failure_location.quote: If $\pi_\tstep$ does not satisfy \cref{reg3}, we may replace $\pi_\tstep$ with  a regularised distribution $\tilde \pi_\tstep$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must prove finite-time error bounds uniform over the family of initial laws used (e.g. uniform bounds on the truncated π_Δt relative to π, or a quantitative bound in ‖ρ0/π‖), control the non-invariance of the truncated law, and give a correct error decomposition.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised convergence of the numerical invariant measure π_Δt to π is not established.
issues.title: Invariant-measure convergence applies the finite-time result to Δt-dependent initial laws without the needed hypotheses or uniformity
issues.why_classification: A main advertised result lacks a valid proof, and repairing it needs new uniform estimates not available in the paper.
